![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14225256/assets/3b8ef36c29d1babc5c3ccf1d474678a18ed5937b883e026d18d5c7ea1aaaa3f5.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the path along the polar curve $r=3+\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta \,$ for $0\le \theta \le \pi ,$ shown above?
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to arc length over $C$ is equal to the arc length $L$ of $C,$ i.e.,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In polar coordinates, the arc length element $\text{d}s$ is given by

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

So, for a polar curve defined as $r=r(\theta )$ for ${\theta }_{1}\le \theta \le {\theta }_{2},$ we have

$$
L={\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=3+\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=3\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta .
$$

Therefore, the expression for our line integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(3+\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta )^{2}+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3\theta )^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9+6\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡3\theta +9{cos}^{2}⁡3\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9+6\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta +1+8{cos}^{2}⁡3\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{10+6\operatorname{sin}⁡3\theta +8{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
